rho.aliases: density; fluid density; material density; wall density
rho.ambiguity_notes: The symbol rho/ρ may also denote electrical resistivity in electromagnetism; resolve by physical context.

rho.aliases: resistivity; specific electrical resistance; rho notation for electrical resistivity; ρ notation for electrical resistivity
rho.definition: Material property relating electric field to current density; equivalently electrical resistance times a length scale divided by area.
rho.ambiguity_notes: Eta/η may denote dynamic viscosity or magnetic diffusivity; rho/ρ may denote mass density. In an MHD prompt explicitly saying electrical resistivity, use this record.
rho.source: MHD Flow in Simple Cubic Periodic Array Geometry, Journal of Fusion Energy (2023)

rho.definition: Depth of the vapor depression or keyhole formed during intense laser-metal interaction.
rho.source: Gan et al., Universal scaling laws of keyhole stability and porosity in 3D printing of metals, Nature Communications (2021)

Tl-T0.ambiguity_notes: A temperature difference has the same dimension as thermodynamic temperature.

Tl-T0.definition: Depth of the vapor depression or keyhole formed during intense laser-metal interaction.
Tl-T0.source: Gan et al., Universal scaling laws of keyhole stability and porosity in 3D printing of metals, Nature Communications (2021)

Tl-T0.ambiguity_notes: Do not confuse T used for temperature with the base-dimension symbol T used for time in dimensional notation.

r0.definition: Characteristic radius of the incident laser beam.
r0.source: Gan et al., Universal scaling laws of keyhole stability and porosity in 3D printing of metals, Nature Communications (2021)

r0.ambiguity_notes: r may represent pipe roughness height in some datasets; use the physical description.

r0.definition: Depth of the vapor depression or keyhole formed during intense laser-metal interaction.
r0.source: Gan et al., Universal scaling laws of keyhole stability and porosity in 3D printing of metals, Nature Communications (2021)

alpha.definition: Thermal conductivity divided by the product of density and specific heat capacity.
alpha.ambiguity_notes: Alpha/α may instead denote a thermal expansion coefficient; kappa/κ may instead denote thermal conductivity or another diffusivity.

alpha.aliases: coefficient of thermal expansion; thermal expansivity
alpha.definition: Fractional change of a characteristic length or volume per unit temperature change, according to the chosen convention.
alpha.ambiguity_notes: Alpha/α is also widely used for thermal diffusivity. The Rayleigh-Benard context usually uses alpha for thermal expansion coefficient and kappa for thermal diffusivity.

alpha.definition: Depth of the vapor depression or keyhole formed during intense laser-metal interaction.
alpha.source: Gan et al., Universal scaling laws of keyhole stability and porosity in 3D printing of metals, Nature Communications (2021)

etaP.aliases: absorbed laser power; effective laser power
etaP.definition: Laser power after multiplication by an absorptivity factor; absorptivity is dimensionless, so etaP has power dimensions.
etaP.ambiguity_notes: Do not treat eta/η inside etaP as a dimensional viscosity or resistivity; here it is a dimensionless absorptivity.
etaP.source: Gan et al., Universal scaling laws of keyhole stability and porosity in 3D printing of metals, Nature Communications (2021)

etaP.definition: Depth of the vapor depression or keyhole formed during intense laser-metal interaction.
etaP.source: Gan et al., Universal scaling laws of keyhole stability and porosity in 3D printing of metals, Nature Communications (2021)

etaP.ambiguity_notes: A temperature difference has the same dimension as thermodynamic temperature.

cp.aliases: specific heat; heat capacity per unit mass
cp.ambiguity_notes: Cp can also denote pressure coefficient in fluid mechanics; lowercase cp/c_p usually denotes specific heat capacity.

cp.definition: Specific heat capacity evaluated at constant pressure.
cp.source: Lupi, Heat Transfer, in Fundamentals of Electroheat

cp.definition: Depth of the vapor depression or keyhole formed during intense laser-metal interaction.
cp.source: Gan et al., Universal scaling laws of keyhole stability and porosity in 3D printing of metals, Nature Communications (2021)

Vs.definition: Translation speed of a laser beam relative to the material.
Vs.source: Gan et al., Universal scaling laws of keyhole stability and porosity in 3D printing of metals, Nature Communications (2021)

Vs.definition: Depth of the vapor depression or keyhole formed during intense laser-metal interaction.
Vs.source: Gan et al., Universal scaling laws of keyhole stability and porosity in 3D printing of metals, Nature Communications (2021)

Vs.ambiguity_notes: A temperature difference has the same dimension as thermodynamic temperature.
